chunks.text: SCALE WITH AI Page 1 SCALE WITH AI WELCOME ADDRESS & SESSION INTRODUCTION Good morning, everyone, and a very warm welcome to Scale With AI! First of all, thank you for taking the time to be here today. We understand that as business owners and professionals, your time is extremely valuable, and our endeavour today is to make these few hours meaningful and useful for you. Before we begin, let me briefly share what you can expect from today's session. We all know that running a business comes with its own challenges. Whether it is generating leads, responding to customer enquiries, managing employees, handling daily operations, maintaining follow-ups or making important decisions, there is always something that demands our attention. And this is exactly where AI can make a difference. SO, WHAT ARE WE GOING TO EXPLORE TODAY? We have designed today's programme in a very practical way. 1. First, we will understand AI. We will introduce you to different AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, understand their capabilities and learn which tool is suitable for which task.

This will help everyone concentrate and ensure a comfortable learning environment. If something is urgent, you are welcome to step outside to attend to it. Please feel free to ask questions and share your business challenges. You don't need any prior technical knowledge or experience with AI. We will take you through everything step by step. With that, let's begin today's learning journey. It is now my pleasure to invite our Senior AI Consultant, Mr. Kunal Kishore, to take us forward and guide us through today's session. Page 1 HR Department Knowledge Base Employee policies, procedures and FAQs | Document ID: HR-KB-001 | Version 1.0 TEST DATA NOTICE: This generic sample is intended to test document retrieval, department-level access and RAG question answering. It is not legal advice or an approved employer policy. Replace all examples with your organisation’s approved rules before operational use. 1. Purpose, scope and confidentiality The Human Resources (HR) Department supports recruitment, onboarding, attendance, leave administration, employee records, payroll coordination, performance processes and workplace concerns. This knowledge base is intended for HR personnel and employees who have been granted access to the relevant HR information. Confidentiality: Employee records, compensation, identity documents, medical information, disciplinary records and individual grievances are confidential. Access must be restricted to authorised roles on a need-to-know basis. Employees may access their own permitted records; managers may access information required for their managerial duties; HR personnel may access records according to assigned permissions. 2. Recruitment and selection  A hiring manager raises a role

on a need-to-know basis. Employees may access their own permitted records; managers may access information required for their managerial duties; HR personnel may access records according to assigned permissions. 2. Recruitment and selection  A hiring manager raises a role request stating job title, department, responsibilities, required skills, experience and budget approval.  HR verifies the required approval before circulating the vacancy.  Candidates are assessed against job-related criteria. Interviews, assessments and reference checks may be used where appropriate and lawful.  HR communicates outcomes and retains recruitment records under the organisation’s retention schedule.  An offer should specify role, reporting manager, location, start date, compensation structure and applicable conditions. 3. Joining and onboarding New employees complete joining forms and submit documents requested by HR. These may include identity/address proof, education or experience records, bank details for payroll, tax declarations and signed employment documents. HR verifies documents, creates the employee record, coordinates system access and explains workplace policies. Credentials must be issued securely and never shared. The manager explains the role, team structure, initial priorities, work processes and key contacts.

The manager explains the role, team structure, initial priorities, work processes and key contacts. HR records completion of required induction and policy acknowledgements. 4. Attendance and working hours Employees follow the schedule communicated by their employer or department and record attendance through the designated system. If attendance is missed or a system issue occurs, the employee should promptly notify the manager and HR with the date and details. Corrections require review and approval under the organisation’s process. Employees should notify their manager as early as reasonably possible about lateness or absence. Repeated unexplained absence or inaccurate records may be referred to HR. Remote work, shifts, overtime and compensatory-off arrangements follow separately approved rules. 5. Leave administration Leave requests should be submitted through the designated portal or process, specifying dates, leave type and handover arrangements where relevant. Planned leave should be requested in advance. For illness or emergencies, notify the manager as soon as practicable

Leave administration Leave requests should be submitted through the designated portal or process, specifying dates, leave type and handover arrangements where relevant. Planned leave should be requested in advance. For illness or emergencies, notify the manager as soon as practicable and complete the required record when able. The manager reviews team coverage; HR checks the balance and applicable rules. Leave type Illustrative process Annual / earned Request in advance; subject to balance, policy and team coverage. Sick Notify manager promptly. Documentation may be requested where permitted by policy and law. Casual / personal For short personal needs, subject to applicable rules and approval. Unpaid May be considered when paid leave is unavailable or in other approved cases; authorisation required. Note: These are categories, not guaranteed leave-day entitlements. Actual days, carry-forward, encashment, documentation and approvals must follow the employer’s approved policy and applicable law.

HR DEPARTMENT | KNOWLEDGE BASE Illustrative sample for RAG testing — not an approved company policy. Page 2 6. Payroll, salary and benefits Payroll uses approved employee master data, attendance inputs, authorised leave records, compensation components and applicable deductions. Employees should report discrepancies to HR or Payroll through the official channel, stating the pay period and issue. Payslips and individual compensation information are confidential. Changes to bank details, tax declarations, personal information or compensation must follow the approved process and required verification. HR must not disclose another employee’s salary, bank details, tax information or benefits unless an authorised business or legal requirement applies. 7. Performance and development Performance reviews may consider agreed objectives, work quality, role-specific competencies, collaboration, reliability and outcomes. Managers communicate expectations, provide feedback and document review discussions. Employees may add comments or request clarification. Ratings, promotions, increments and development opportunities follow the organisation’s approved framework and authorised decisions; no outcome is guaranteed by this sample. 8. and development opportunities follow the organisation’s approved framework and authorised decisions; no outcome is guaranteed by this sample. 8. Code of conduct and workplace concerns Employees should act professionally, treat colleagues respectfully, protect confidential information, use company assets responsibly, avoid conflicts of interest and follow workplace rules. Harassment, discrimination, retaliation, threats, fraud, deliberate data misuse and unauthorised disclosure should be reported through the designated grievance, ethics or compliance channel. Reports should be handled discreetly and fairly on a need-to-know basis. Retaliation for a good-faith report is unacceptable. 9. Frequently asked questions Q: Who approves my leave? A: The reporting manager reviews the request; HR checks balance and applicable policy. The official workflow determines final approval. Q: I forgot to mark attendance. What should I do? A: Notify your manager and HR promptly, provide the date and details, and follow the correction process. Do not alter records yourself. Q: Can I ask HR for another employee’s salary? A: No. Individual compensation is confidential and available only to the employee and specifically authorised personnel. Q: Where do I report workplace misconduct? A:

correction process. Do not alter records yourself. Q: Can I ask HR for another employee’s salary? A: No. Individual compensation is confidential and available only to the employee and specifically authorised personnel. Q: Where do I report workplace misconduct? A: Use the organisation’s designated HR grievance, ethics or compliance channel. For immediate danger, contact the appropriate emergency or safety resource. Q: Which leave balance or salary applies to me? A: Check your authenticated employee record or contact authorised HR/Payroll staff. This general document contains no individual employee data. 10. RAG access-control metadata Suggested metadata: department=HR; classification=internal-confidential; allowed_groups=HR_Admin,HR_Staff. Employee self-service should be enabled only for separately permission-filtered personal records. Do not automatically grant all employees access to internal HR procedures. For reliable isolation, create separate documents for employee-facing guidance, HR-only procedures and individual employee records. Apply permissions at document and chunk level, preserve metadata during ingestion, and filter retrieval using the authenticated user’s verified department and role. Sample Executive Role Knowledge Base — For RAG Testing Page 1 of 2 EXECUTIVE ROLE — OPERATING GUIDELINES RAG TEST KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT | Version 1.0 | Effective date: 1 October 2026 | Document owner: People & Operations 1. Role purpose The Executive is responsible for coordinating day-to-day business operations, translating approved plans into action, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring that assigned work is completed on time. The role supports managers and senior leaders by preparing reliable information, tracking commitments, communicating with relevant stakeholders, and escalating issues that exceed the Executive’s authority. The Executive is expected to demonstrate sound judgement, confidentiality, ownership, clear written and verbal communication, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities. The role does not independently change company strategy, approve unbudgeted expenditure, or make commitments on behalf of the organisation unless written authority has been delegated. 2. Core responsibilities Planning and coordination: Maintain task lists, meeting calendars, action trackers, and delivery timelines. Confirm owners and due dates after meetings. Notify the relevant manager when a dependency or deadline is at risk. Reporting and documentation: Prepare

delegated. 2. Core responsibilities Planning and coordination: Maintain task lists, meeting calendars, action trackers, and delivery timelines. Confirm owners and due dates after meetings. Notify the relevant manager when a dependency or deadline is at risk. Reporting and documentation: Prepare weekly status updates using verified information. Check figures against the approved source before circulation. Store final documents in the designated shared repository and use the current approved template. Stakeholder communication: Respond to routine internal and external requests within one business day. Acknowledge requests that require research and provide an expected response date. Use professional, factual language and do not speculate about unapproved decisions. Process and service support: Follow documented procedures, identify recurring process delays, and suggest practical improvements. Record incidents and customer or employee concerns in the appropriate system. Confidentiality and data handling: Share information only with people who have a business need and appropriate access. Do not send confidential files to personal email accounts or unapproved external services. Report suspected loss, misdirection, or unauthorised access immediately to the line manager and Information Security. 3. Decision rights and approval limits

a business need and appropriate access. Do not send confidential files to personal email accounts or unapproved external services. Report suspected loss, misdirection, or unauthorised access immediately to the line manager and Information Security. 3. Decision rights and approval limits The Executive may organise work within an approved plan, request routine information from relevant teams, schedule meetings, and correct obvious formatting or clerical errors. The Executive may not approve new suppliers, sign contracts, change employee compensation, make public statements, or approve expenditure outside a formally delegated limit. Activity Executive authority Required approval / escalation Routine operating purchase within an assigned budget May process only where written delegation exists Line manager or budget owner if delegation is absent Unbudgeted spend or purchase above delegated limit No approval authority Budget owner and Finance Contract, legal commitment, or supplier appointment May coordinate documentation only Authorised signatory and Procurement / Legal External statement on company position May share approved published information Communications lead or designated spokesperson

Sample Executive Role Knowledge Base — For RAG Testing Page 2 of 2 EXECUTIVE ROLE — PERFORMANCE & ESCALATION RAG TEST KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT | Version 1.0 | Effective date: 1 October 2026 4. Performance measures Performance is reviewed monthly by the line manager. The following measures are standard role indicators; any role-specific targets documented in the employee’s approved objectives take precedence. Measure Standard target How it is measured Task completion At least 95% completed by agreed due date Completed on-time tasks ÷ tasks due in the month Routine request acknowledgement Within 1 business day Timestamp of receipt compared with first acknowledgement Weekly status report Submitted by 12:00 noon each Friday Submission timestamp and completeness check Record accuracy At least 98% accuracy in sampled records Monthly sample reviewed by the line manager Meeting action tracking Actions circulated within 1 business day Time between meeting end and distribution of action log 5. RAG status definitions and escalation Green: Work is on track, the owner is clear, and the agreed deadline is achievable. Continue normal monitoring and include progress in the weekly update.

Time between meeting end and distribution of action log 5. RAG status definitions and escalation Green: Work is on track, the owner is clear, and the agreed deadline is achievable. Continue normal monitoring and include progress in the weekly update. Amber: There is a credible risk to timing, quality, budget, or dependency, but recovery is still possible. The Executive must notify the task owner and line manager as soon as the risk is identified, state the likely impact, and propose a recovery action. Amber items must appear in the weekly status report with an owner and next review date. Red: A deadline has been missed, a material service or compliance issue has occurred, a critical dependency has failed, or recovery is not currently achievable. Escalate immediately to the line manager. For suspected data breaches, safety incidents, fraud, or legal issues, use the relevant urgent reporting channel without waiting for the weekly meeting. A RAG rating must reflect evidence, not optimism. If information is incomplete, mark the item Amber and state what is unknown. Do not mark an item Green solely

use the relevant urgent reporting channel without waiting for the weekly meeting. A RAG rating must reflect evidence, not optimism. If information is incomplete, mark the item Amber and state what is unknown. Do not mark an item Green solely because no one has reported a problem. 6. Reporting cadence and response expectations  Daily: Review priorities, deadlines, meetings, and urgent messages at the start of the working day.  Weekly: Submit the status report by Friday 12:00 noon; include completed work, upcoming milestones, Amber and Red risks, decisions required, and overdue actions.  Monthly: Review performance measures and recurring process issues with the line manager.  Urgent issue: Contact the line manager immediately through the approved channel; do not wait for the next scheduled report. 7. Example scenarios for knowledge retrieval Scenario A: A task due tomorrow depends on data from another team, and that team has not confirmed delivery. Expected response: Amber; contact the dependency owner and line manager, document the impact, and agree a next review date. Scenario B: A report contains a suspected material error after

data from another team, and that team has not confirmed delivery. Expected response: Amber; contact the dependency owner and line manager, document the impact, and agree a next review date. Scenario B: A report contains a suspected material error after it has been circulated. Expected response: Notify the line manager promptly, verify the correct figure against the source, and issue a clearly labelled correction through the approved channel. Scenario C: An external party asks the Executive to confirm an unannounced company decision. Expected response: Do not speculate or confirm. Refer the request to the designated spokesperson or Communications lead. 8. Document control This document is a sample operational reference created for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) testing. It is not a substitute for an organisation’s employment contract, financial delegation schedule, security policy, or approved standard operating procedures. Where another approved policy conflicts with this sample, the approved policy takes precedence.

Sample Finance Role Knowledge Base — For RAG Testing Page 1 of 2 FINANCE ROLE — OPERATING GUIDELINES RAG TEST KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT | Version 1.0 | Effective date: 1 October 2026 | Document owner: Finance 1. Role purpose The Finance Executive supports the organisation’s financial control and reporting activities by processing and reviewing financial information, maintaining accurate records, supporting payment and collection workflows, and helping ensure that transactions are complete, authorised, and recorded in the correct period. The role provides timely, evidence-based information to the Finance Manager and relevant business teams. The role requires integrity, confidentiality, numerical accuracy, attention to detail, professional communication, and adherence to approved financial policies. The Finance Executive must not create fictitious records, bypass approval controls, share financial data without authorisation, or make commitments outside delegated authority. 2. Core responsibilities Accounts payable: Receive supplier invoices, check supplier details and supporting documents, verify purchase order or service confirmation where required, identify duplicate or inconsistent invoices, and route items for approval before payment processing. Accounts receivable: Prepare or coordinate customer invoices using approved terms, record receipts against the

supplier details and supporting documents, verify purchase order or service confirmation where required, identify duplicate or inconsistent invoices, and route items for approval before payment processing. Accounts receivable: Prepare or coordinate customer invoices using approved terms, record receipts against the correct customer account, monitor overdue balances, and follow the approved reminder and escalation process. Reconciliations: Prepare assigned bank, ledger, supplier, customer, or expense reconciliations. Investigate differences, retain supporting evidence, and escalate unresolved or unusual items to the Finance Manager. Expense and reimbursement support: Check claims for required receipts, business purpose, policy compliance, and approval. Return incomplete claims for correction; do not approve a claim unless approval authority has been formally delegated. Month-end support: Complete assigned schedules by the close calendar, check that entries have appropriate support, flag missing accruals or unusual movements, and assist with documentation for review. Journal entries must be reviewed and approved according to the delegation matrix. Financial records and confidentiality: Store invoices, vouchers, reconciliations, and reports in the approved finance repository. Restrict access to authorised users. Do not share bank details, payroll information, customer data, or

must be reviewed and approved according to the delegation matrix. Financial records and confidentiality: Store invoices, vouchers, reconciliations, and reports in the approved finance repository. Restrict access to authorised users. Do not share bank details, payroll information, customer data, or financial statements externally without approval. 3. Controls and approval limits The Finance Executive may perform assigned processing, checking, reconciliation, and reporting tasks. Processing a transaction is not the same as approving it. The Executive must follow segregation-of-duties controls and must not approve their own expenses, create and release the same payment where prohibited, or alter supplier bank details without independent verification. Activity Finance Executive may Approval / escalation Invoice processing Check documentation and enter approved invoices Budget owner / authorised invoice approver Supplier payment Prepare payment proposal and supporting file Authorised payment releaser under bank mandate Expense reimbursement Check claim completeness and policy compliance Employee’s authorised manager; Finance review as required Journal entry Prepare draft with evidence and explanation Independent reviewer / authorised Finance approver Supplier bank-detail change Initiate verification using approved contact details Independent verification and authorised master-data approver

Performance measures Performance is reviewed monthly by the Finance Manager. These are sample operating targets for RAG testing; organisation-specific targets, accounting policies, statutory requirements, and approved close calendars take precedence. Measure Sample target How it is measured Invoice processing accuracy At least 98% in monthly sample Invoices without processing or coding errors ÷ invoices sampled Invoice workflow turnaround Within 3 business days after complete documentation and approvals Receipt of complete file to completion of assigned processing Reconciliation completion 100% of assigned reconciliations by close-calendar deadline Completed and reviewed reconciliations against monthly schedule Unresolved reconciling items All items investigated and assigned an owner / action date Ageing and status of open items in reconciliation tracker Record retention 100% of sampled transactions have required supporting evidence Monthly sample of transaction files and repository records 5. RAG status definitions and escalation Green: The transaction or deliverable is complete or on

status of open items in reconciliation tracker Record retention 100% of sampled transactions have required supporting evidence Monthly sample of transaction files and repository records 5. RAG status definitions and escalation Green: The transaction or deliverable is complete or on track; required documents and approvals are available; reconciliations have no unexplained material differences; and the deadline is achievable. Amber: A document or approval is pending, a reconciliation difference remains under investigation, an invoice or close task may miss its deadline, or an unusual transaction requires clarification. Notify the Finance Manager or assigned owner promptly, record the amount and potential impact where known, and agree an owner and next review date. Red: There is suspected fraud, duplicate or unauthorised payment, material unexplained variance, missed statutory or critical close deadline, suspected data breach, or evidence that a financial control has been bypassed. Escalate immediately through the approved Finance, Compliance, Information Security, or incident-reporting channel. Do not conceal, overwrite, or independently resolve suspected misconduct. Escalate immediately through the approved Finance, Compliance, Information Security, or incident-reporting channel. Do not conceal, overwrite, or independently resolve suspected misconduct. RAG ratings must be based on evidence. If the amount, cause, or impact is not yet known, state that it is unconfirmed and identify the next investigation step. Do not mark an item Green merely because no issue has been reported. 6. Reporting cadence and response expectations  Daily: Review invoice queues, payment or collection items assigned, urgent queries, and exceptions.  Weekly: Update the AP / AR ageing or work tracker, unresolved reconciliation items, and risks requiring management attention.  Month-end: Complete assigned close tasks and reconciliations by the approved close calendar; submit supporting schedules for review.  Urgent issue: Escalate suspected fraud, unauthorised payment, incorrect bank-detail change, control override, or data exposure immediately. 7. Example scenarios for knowledge retrieval Scenario A: A supplier emails new bank details and asks for an urgent payment. Expected response: Do not update the master record based only on the email. Follow the approved independent verification process using previously validated contact information

knowledge retrieval Scenario A: A supplier emails new bank details and asks for an urgent payment. Expected response: Do not update the master record based only on the email. Follow the approved independent verification process using previously validated contact information and obtain the required authorisation. Scenario B: A bank reconciliation contains an unexplained difference at month-end. Expected response: Investigate using transaction evidence, record the difference and potential impact, assign an owner and action date, and escalate if it remains unresolved or appears material. Scenario C: An employee submits an expense claim without a receipt or required approval. Expected response: Return the claim for missing evidence or approval. Do not process it as approved or waive policy requirements without authorised exception approval.
